question.problem: Determine the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{x+5}{{x}^{2}-x-2}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{2}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x+5}{{x}^{2}-x-2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{x}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{x}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})}{(1-\frac{1}{x}-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{1}{x},\frac{5}{{x}^{2}}$ and $\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})}{(1-\frac{1}{x}-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & \to \frac{0+0}{1-0-0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y=0.$
